question: An engineer asks your agent to review a legacy billing module of 16 files before a shared library upgrade. The review must find deprecated library calls in each file. It must also find data that one file passes to another file in a format that the receiving file no longer accepts. A single review pass over all 16 files missed deprecated calls in the later files and found no cross-file mismatches. Which design of the review best fixes both problems?

options.text: Run a focused pass for each file, and give each pass the full text of all 16 files so it can check data exchange.
options.reason: Each pass would load all 16 files, so it would no longer be focused and attention would be diluted again. The guide puts cross-file checks in a separate integration pass instead.

options.text: Chain a focused pass for each file that reports its local deprecated calls, then a separate integration pass that checks the data passed between the files.
options.reason: Per-file local passes avoid attention dilution. The separate cross-file integration pass then catches the mismatches between files, so this design fixes both problems.

options.text: Split the single pass into two passes over all 16 files, one that looks for deprecated calls and one that looks for data mismatches.
options.reason: Each pass still covers all 16 files at once, so attention stays diluted. Later files can still get shallow analysis.

options.text: Run a focused pass for each file and join the 16 reports, with no later pass that examines how the files exchange data.
options.reason: The per-file passes fix the shallow analysis. Without a cross-file integration pass, however, nothing checks the data passed between files, so the mismatches stay hidden.
